MINUTES
  MALIBU PUBLIC SAFETY COMMISSION
  ADJOURNED REGULAR MEETING
  JULY 12, 2023
  TELECONFERENCED VARIOUS LOCATIONS
  5:00 P.M.

The following meeting was held pursuant to AB 361 and fully teleconferenced from various
locations during the coronavirus disease (COVID-19) pandemic.

CALL TO ORDER

  Chair Frost called the meeting to order at 5:03 p.m.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Chair Chris Frost; Vice Chair Joshua Spiegel; Commissioners Keegan Gibbs,
  and Brian Merrick; and Ex Officio Member Brent Woodworth (arrived at 6:06 p.m.)

  ABSENT:  Commissioner Daphne Anneet

  ALSO PRESENT:  Susan Dueflas, Public Safety Director; Rob DuBoux, Public Works
  Director; Luis Flores, Public Safety Liaison; Sarah Flores, Emergency Services
  Coordinator; Gabe Etcheverry, Fire Safety Liaison; Brad Yocum, Fire Safety Liaison;
  Arthur Aladjadjian, Public Works Superintendent; Parker Davis, Media Technician;
  Sergeant Christopher Soderlund, Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department; and Mary
  Linden, Executive Assistant

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Commissioner Gibbs led the Pledge of Allegiance.

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

MOTION  Commissioner Gibbs moved, and Vice Chair Spiegel seconded a motion to approve
  the agenda. The question was called, and the motion carried 4-0, Commissioner
  Anneet absent.

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  Executive Assistant Linden reported that the agenda for the meeting was properly posted
  on July 5, 2023.

ITEM 1  CEREMONIAL / PRESENTATIONS

  None.
 Malibu Public Safety Commission
Adjourned Regular Meeting
Minutes of July 12, 2023
Page 2 of 8

ITEM 2.A.  PUBLIC COMMENTS

  None.

ITEM 2.B.  STAFF UPDATES

  Public Safety Director Dueflas stated the school safety assessment first draft was
  received. She stated it had good, constructive recommendations for access control.
  She stated the final draft would be released soon. She stated the Sheriffs service
  agreement was put in place. She discussed staffing shortages. She stated service
  levels mirrored last year. She stated the City and Sheriffs Department (LASD)
  would meet next week about the Sheriffs substation. She stated the Volunteers on
  Patrol (VOP) car bailment agreement was approved by the Los Angeles County
  Board of Supervisors at the end of June. She stated the car would hopefully be in
  service by the end of next month.

  Public Safety Liaison Flores reported that 58 vehicles were towed over the July 4
  holiday weekend and six more over the past weekend bringing the total to over 200
  cars towed so far this summer. He discussed a few vehicles that were removed in
  the past few weeks. He announced that staff, the homeless outreach team, and
  volunteers would conduct a summer homeless count tomorrow morning. He stated
  a Southern California Edison (SCE) license was being reviewed by the City
  Attorney’s office, which was the last step before automatic license plate reader
  (ALPR) cameras could be installed.

  Fire Safety Liaison Etcheverry stated Live Fuel Moisture (LFM) levels were at
  92%. He stated the historic average was 90%. He stated the past two years averaged
  much lower at this time of year due to ongoing drought conditions. He stated 29 of
  30 beacon boxes with maps had been installed, and the vendor indicated the final
  17 boxes ordered would arrive soon.

  Fire Safety Liaison Yocum stated the Fire Safety Liaisons (FSL) were working with
  neighborhoods within the city limits to join a fire wise community in Malibu.

  Fire Safety Liaison Vandermeulen stated the FSL attended the Susana Mutual
  Threat Zone Workshop. In response to Chair Frost, Fire Safety Liaison
  Vandermeulen confirmed the zone included the watershed area where the Woolsey
  Fire started.

  Emergency Services Coordinator Flores discussed National Preparedness Month
  activities scheduled in September. She stated postcards regarding new evacuation
  zones will be going out to all residents. She commended Community Emergency
  Response Team (CERT) members for their participation in emergency
  preparedness events and assistance with CERT training.
 Malibu Public Safety Commission
Adjourned Regular Meeting
Minutes of July 12, 2023
Page 3 of 8

  Public Safety Director Dueñas stated she was looking into options for increasing
  parking enforcement.

  Fire Safety Liaison Vandermeulen stated the home hardening classes on June 14
  and June 15 were very successful with 27 people attending. He stated another class
  would hopefully be offered by the end of August.

  Chair Frost stated he attended the class and that it was extremely informative.

  Public Works Director DuBoux discussed flooding in the undercrossing at Busch
  Drive and PCH resulting in its closure over the July 4 holiday weekend. He stated
  directional signs were in place at the Arizona crossing at Westward Beach to direct
  motorists to beach parking. He discussed projects on PCH scheduled over the next
  six to eight months, including a protected left turn at Las Flores Canyon Road, the
  undercrossing near Corral Canyon, and the PCH Signal Synchronization Project.

  In response to Commissioner Merrick, Public Works Director DuBoux confirmed
  the Arizona crossing was no longer open after the holiday ended.

  In response to Chair Frost, Public Works Director DuBoux stated he was
  collaborating with the County of Los Angeles and its Department of Beaches and
  Harbors for final resolution about the underpass by Zuma Beach.

  Public Works Superintendent Aladjadjian stated Caltrans had issued an emergency
  contract to clear debris on PCH caused by storm activity earlier in the year. He
  stated street sweeping had been increased in preparation for the holiday weekend.
  In response to Commissioner Gibbs, Public Works Superintendent Aladjadjian
  discussed debris removal along the shoulders near Las Flores Canyon Road and
  Big Rock Drive.

ITEM 2.C.  COMMISSIONER COMMENTS

  Commissioner Gibbs asked what ~he requirements were for a fire wise community.
  Fire Safety Liaison Yocum stated arisk assessment had to be conducted for each
  area and a leader selected. He stated the City’s FSL would be trained in how to do
  therisk assessmçnt. Commissioner Gibbs stated he was interested in helping to get
  the community involved.

  Commissioner Merrick, stated many people were very unhappy about sitting in
  traffic because of an event at Nobu.

  Vice Chair Spiegel stated he was glad the VOP car would be ready soon. He stated
  a car should be on hand to in~mediately replace a damaged car. He suggested
  beginning now to approve a new v~hicle. Public Safety Director Dueflas stated she
  requested another car in the Fiscal Year 2023~24 budget.
 Malibu Public Safety Commission
Adjourned Regular Meeting
Minutes of July 12, 2023
Page 4 of 8

  In response to Chair Frost, Public Works Director DuBoux stated the City was
  working with the insurance company to possibly receive reimbursement for the car.

  Vice Chair Spiegel commended staff for getting almost all the Beacon boxes up
  and running. He suggested inspecting the locks regularly due to damage from damp
  sea air. Fire Safety Liaison Etcheverry stated the locks were intended to just keep
  the public out and would be cut off by fire personnel when needed.

  Vice Chair Spiegel stated the holiday weekend was pretty good. He stated it was
  time for the City to flex its muscles with Nobu. He suggested the Commission
  consider revisiting the nuisance ordinance or increase fines.

  Public Safety Director Dueñas stated much was happening with City management
  and staff to address the Nobu issues.

  Vice Chair Spiegel announced the goats were back in Malibu West for brush
  clearance. He stated he hoped other communities would consider using goats.

  Commissioner Gibbs agreed with Vice Chair Spiegel that the Commission should
  be involved in discussion of resolutions for the Nobu issues. He agreed with Vice
  Chair Spiegel that the goats made a significant impact on fuel and vegetation health.

  Chair Frost stated he talked with the Fire Department about getting a Fire Safety
  Officer (FSO) at Nobu’s expense during peak weekends and holidays. He stated it
  was also a traffic problem. He discussed a bonfire in the Point Dume headlands late
  one night over the holiday weekend. He discussed a confrontation between the
  owner of a problem recreational vehicle (RV) and some permitted vendors. He
  commended the City’s efforts related to homelessness. He stated the Sheriffs
  Department will monitor the ALPR. Sergeant Soderlund stated they were looking
  at multiple options. Chair Frost stated SCE responded quickly to reports of lights
  out on Westward Beach Road. He commended the FSL and Sergeant Soderlund, as
  well as Public Safety Department and Public Works Department staff

ITEM 3  CONSENT CALENDAR

MOTION  Vice Chair Spiegel moved, and Chair Frost seconded a motion to approve the
  Consent Calendar. The question was called, and the motion carried 4-0,
  Commissioner Anneet absent.

  The Consent Calendar consisted of the following items:

  A.  Previously Discussed Items
  None.
  B.  New Items
  1.  Approval of Minutes May 3, 2023 Public Works Commission and Public
  —

  Safety Commission Joint Special Meeting
 Malibu Public Safety Commission
Adjourned Regular Meeting
Minutes of July 12, 2023

  Recommended Action:  Approve minutes for the Public Works
  Commission and Public Safety Commission Joint Special meeting of May
  3, 2023.
  2.  Approval of Minutes June 7, 2023
  —

  Recommended Action: Approve minutes for the Public Safety Commission
  Regular meeting of June 7, 2023.
  3.  Public Safety Commission Assignments for Fiscal Year (FY) 2023-24
  Recommended Action: Receive and file the Public Safety Commission
  Assignments for FY 2023-24 approved by the City Council on June 26,
  2023.

ITEM 4  OLD BUSINESS

  None.

ITEM 5  NEW BUSINESS

  A.  Speeding in Canyon Neighborhoods

  Recommended Action: 1) Review public safety concerns due to speeding in Las
  Flores Canyon and Rambla Pacifico Street; 2) Receive a report on enforcement and
  speed calming measures; and 3) Make a recommendation to the City Council if
  appropriate.

  Public Safety Director Duefias introduced the report. She stated the California
  Highway Patrol (CHP) Street Racing Enforcement Sergeant had planned to attend
  but had to cancel. She stated CHP, like LASD, was very short-staffed.

  Public Works Director DuBoux presented the report on traffic calming measures.
  He explained the City’s speed hump policy.

  Public Works Superintendent Aladjadjian discussed the City’s determination for
  not permitting speed humps requested for Las Flores Canyon Road. He stated other
  traffic calming measures were recommended, including signage, striping, and
  stenciling on the roadway. He stated the City was investigating speed hump
  requests for Bonsall Drive and upper Busch Drive.

  In response to Chair Frost, Public Works Superintendent Aladjadjian confirmed
  speed humps could not be installed above a six percent grade.

  Sergeant Soderlund discussed where enforcement was provided by the Sheriffs
  Department and CHP. He stated a CHP Street Racing motorcycle officer provided
  a briefing at the Lost Hills Station about enforcing modified vehicles. He stated
  deputies were limited to enforcing only within the city limits. He discussed AB 645,
  proposed legislation for a five-year pilot program to install speed cameras in areas
  where speeding was a serious issue. He stated the Los Angeles County Board of
 Malibu Public Safety Commission
Adjourned Regular Meeting
Minutes of July 12, 2023
Page 6 of 8

  Supervisors just approved funding for Safe Canyons overtime, which would fund
  traffic deputies in the canyons.

  Ex Officio Member Woodworth arrived at 6:06 p.m.

  Birute Anne Vileisis stated she has lived on Schueren Road at the top of Las Flores
  Canyon for 36 years. She discussed an increase in speeding over the past three to
  five years. She stated it was no longer safe to walk there. She discussed many cars
  running the red light at PCH and Las Flores Canyon Road. She discussed getting
  caught in traffic due to the Nobu event on July 4. She stated limousines were using
  the center divider.

  Marcia Loots-Serna expressed support for speed cameras. She asked if a speed
  force could be organized or lookouts at the tops of canyon roads. She expressed
  concern that speed cameras would be destroyed. She asked how many fatalities
  occurred each year on the five canyon roads.

  Sergeant Soderlund stated he could collect statistics for incidents within the Malibu
  city limits. He stated actions could only be taken if a deputy observed the violation.
  In response to Public Safety Director Dueflas, Sergeant Soderlund stated AB 645
  was only a pilot program to check effectiveness before considering applying it
  statewide. He stated warnings would be issued in the first 60 days with fines
  imposed after that.

  Chair Frost stated tickets for the camera program would go to the registered owner
  who may not be driving the vehicle.

  Commissioner Gibbs thanked the speakers for attending. He discussed the Sheriffs
  Department contract for enforcement only within the Malibu city limits. In response
  to Commissioner Gibbs, Sergeant Soderlund confirmed enforcement in
  unincorporated areas was under CHP jurisdiction. Commissioner Gibbs suggested
  the speakers bring their concerns to CHP. He discussed an upcoming Caltrans
  project to update the intersections of PCH at Las Flores Canyon Road and Rambla
  Pacifico.

  Public Works Director DuBoux stated Caltrans and the City were collaborating on
  projects to improve safety at those intersections.

  Commissioner Merrick suggested adding flashing school zone speed limit signs or
  rumble strips to slow traffic on Las Flores Canyon Road. Public Works
  Superintendent Aladjadjian stated he would have the traffic engineer look into those
  suggestions. He stated some residents complained about noise from rumble strips
  or dots on the road.

  Ex Officio Member Woodworth thanked the speakers. He asked if a meeting could
  be scheduled with CHP, LASD, and the residents to discuss their concerns.
 Malibu Public Safety Commission
Adjourned Regular Meeting
Minutes of July 12, 2023
Page 7 of 8

  Sergeant Soderlund stated he would try to. facilitate a meeting. He stated the CHP
  West Valley station covered that area as well as the 101, 405, and 118 freeways so
  resources were often diverted to the freeways.

  B.  Homelessness Task Force Assignment Transfer

  Recommended Action: 1) Review the Homelessness Task Force Charter and its
  assignments; and 2) Identify how to proceed with remaining assignments per the
  City Council’s direction.

  Public Safety Liaison Flores presented the report.

  Terry Davis commended the Public Safety Commission and Public Works
  Commission. She discussed the Homelessness Task Force (HTF) Fire, Health and
  Public Safety Ad Hoc Committee’s last report submitted to the City Council with
  suggestions related to public education. She stated Malibu Community Assistance
  Resource Team (C.A.R.T.) could be a liaison with staff.

  Vice Chair Spiegel stated the HTF did a lot of good work. In response to Vice Chair
  Spiegel, Public Safety Director Dueñas discussed how the tasks could be requested
  by the Commission for upcoming agendas. Vice Chair Spiegel thanked Ms. Davis
  for her work. He stated he did not want to lose momentum.

  Chair Frost agreed with Vice Chair Spiegel. He agreed with Public Safety Director
  Dueñas’ suggestion, which would streamline the work.

  Public Safety Director Dueflas stated staff could commit to bring back at least one
  task each month. Public Safety Liaison Flores stated staff could prioritize the tasks
  for the Commission to address.

  Commissioner Merrick stated he was not up to speed on the issues and what had
  been done by the HTF.

  Commissioner Gibbs stated he was in the same place as Commissioner Merrick.

  Ex Officio Member Woodworth agreed that this was a critical problem throughout
  Southern California. He stated he would like to learn more about the issues specific
  to Malibu.

  Commissioner Gibbs thanked everyone who worked on the HTF.

  C.  Public Safety Agency Activity
  Recommended Action: Discuss recent Public Safety Agency activities and receive
  and file activity reports from the County of Los Angeles Sheriff’s Department, Fire
  Department, and Lifeguard Division.
 Malibu Public Safety Commission
Adjourned Regular Meeting
Minutes of July 12, 2023
Page 8 of 8

  Sergeant Soderlund discussed June crime statistics. He stated the 212 year-to-date
  Part 1 crimes compared to 242 at this time in 2022 was a 12.4% decrease since last
  year. He discussed notable incidents in June. He stated a vehicle burglary
  suppression operation was scheduled for next week.

  Chair Frost stated there were reports of fireworks being shot off from on top of the
  post office building at Heathercliff Road.

  Commissioner Gibbs stated cones had previously been placed in the center lane in
  front of Nobu to block traffic. He suggested that be considered again this summer.

  In response to Chair Frost, Public Works Director DuBoux stated the plan to make
  the pedestrian signal near Nobu into a full signal was delayed by the Planning
  Commission. He stated traffic issues would be addressed when Nobu brought its
  valet parking plans to the Planning Commission.

  In response to Commissioner Gibbs, Sergeant Soderlund stated he, Captain Seetoo,
  and some traffic deputies were scheduled to meet with Nobu next week.

  Public Safety Director Dueñas announced the City submitted a letter to LASD
  requesting that Sergeant Soderlund officially be assigned as the Malibu Liaison.

ADJOURNMENT

MOTION  At 7:00 p.m., Chair Frost moved and Commissioner Merrick seconded a motion to
  adjourn. The question was called, and the motion carried 4-0, Commissioner
  Anneet absent.

  Approved and adopted by the P ~j~l1~ afety Commission of the City
  of Malibu on August 2, 2023.
